correctness.rationale: Conditional on two distinct open components, uniform-root first- and second-moment increments are exactly 2ab/n and 3ab(a+b)/n. Expanding the centered second moment gives the displayed exact difference; the all-edges-failed event makes A positive at each interior probability. The p->0 expansions follow from the all-edges-failed event and bounded moments. At mu>=3n/4, a+b<=n makes the expectation nonpositive while the -p^2 A^2 term is strictly negative; connectedness gives mu->n as p->1. The standalone verifier checks 12908 finite labeled graph-edge-probability combinations with exact rational arithmetic, including 5756 high-mean test cases, but universality rests solely on the proof. No unproved lemma or computational extrapolation is needed.

value.rationale: The claim resolves a natural uncertainty-versus-average-size tension for any single contact addition in an otherwise arbitrary finite connected epidemic network: mean final size always rises, yet outbreak-size variance must switch from increasing to decreasing with transmissibility. The explicit 3n/4 sufficient criterion gives a topology-independent diagnostic. This is a universal qualitative boundary, not an arbitrary numerical slice, a standard exercise in monotonicity, or a small finite lookup; the model restriction and nonoptimality of the criterion are disclosed.
